question.text: Which of the following best describes the 'satellite' component of a core-satellite portfolio?

answer.text: Long-term, low-volatility holdings with low turnover
Opportunistic, high-turnover, tactical allocations optimising risk-adjusted return
Passive ETFs on broad-market indices only

explanation.text: The Logic: Satellite aims to enhance return via tactical bets, higher turnover, and active selection — performance is measured on mean-variance optimisation, not tracking error. The Trap: Low turnover and tracking-error goals are CORE characteristics — the question asks for SATELLITE. Cross-Exam Context: Core-satellite is covered at conceptual level in XIX-A; XXI-B expects you to distinguish the performance metrics per sleeve. Manager's Pro-Tip: If the satellite sleeve's holdings stop moving, it's closet-indexing its own sleeve — time to raise questions with the PM.
